Authors: J. Mirkovic and P. Reiher
Title: A taxonomy of DDoS attack and DDoS defense mechanisms
Problem_Addressed: Lack of structured classification of DDoS attack vectors and defense strategies
Method: Conceptual taxonomy and comparative classification framework
Measure_Used: Classification completeness across attack and defense dimensions
Main_Finding: Categorized DDoS attacks by degree of automation, exploited vulnerability, source address validity, and attack rate dynamics
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Pre-dates modern cloud CDNs, IoT botnets, and large-scale UDP amplification

Authors: S. T. Zargar, J. Joshi, and D. Tipper
Title: A survey of defense mechanisms against distributed denial of service (DDoS) flooding attacks
Problem_Addressed: Fragmented understanding of network and application flooding defenses across deployment locations
Method: Literature survey comparing source-end, core-end, victim-end, and distributed defenses
Measure_Used: Deployment location, cooperation requirement, and mitigation overhead
Main_Finding: Distributed defenses coordinated across network points outperform isolated victim-end filtering
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Limited coverage of modern commercial cloud scrubbing and serverless edge mitigation

Authors: O. Osanaiye, K.-K. R. Choo, and M. Dlodlo
Title: Distributed denial of service (DDoS) resilience in cloud: Review and conceptual cloud DDoS mitigation framework
Venue: Journal of Network and Computer Applications
Problem_Addressed: Vulnerability of cloud-hosted services to multi-vector DDoS attacks
Method: Literature review and conceptual change-point detection framework
Measure_Used: Detection responsiveness and cloud resource elasticity
Main_Finding: Cloud elasticity helps absorb bursts, but requires proactive anomaly detection to prevent economic denial of sustainability
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Conceptual framework without live small-operator cost benchmarking

Authors: M. Antonakakis et al.
Title: Understanding the Mirai botnet
Venue: Proceedings of the 26th USENIX Security Symposium
Problem_Addressed: Emergence of massive IoT-driven DDoS attacks capable of disrupting major targets
Method: Empirical measurement using honeypots, sinkholes, and passive DNS/network telemetry
Dataset_or_Testbed: 7 months of longitudinal internet measurement data (2016-2017)
Measure_Used: Infected device count, attack frequency, target distribution
Main_Finding: Compromised consumer IoT devices peaked at ~600,000 bots and launched high-volume attacks against diverse targets
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Focuses on botnet anatomy rather than small-website mitigation economics

Authors: I. Sharafaldin, A. H. Lashkari, S. Hakak, and A. A. Ghorbani
Title: Developing realistic distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack dataset and taxonomy
Venue: Proceedings of the IEEE 53rd International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology
Problem_Addressed: Outdated and unrealistic benchmark datasets for evaluating DDoS classifiers
Method: Testbed traffic generation and machine learning feature evaluation
Dataset_or_Testbed: CICDDoS2019 (12 modern reflection/exploitation DDoS attack types)
Measure_Used: Precision, recall, F1-score across ML classifiers
Main_Finding: Created a widely adopted benchmark dataset and flow feature set for modern reflective DDoS detection
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Controlled lab traffic does not capture production SME web workloads or edge filtering constraints

Authors: S. Ismail, H. R. Hassen, M. Just, and H. Zantout
Title: A review of amplification-based distributed denial of service attacks and their mitigation
Problem_Addressed: Low-cost, high-bandwidth amplification attacks exploiting stateless protocols
Method: Systematic review of amplification vectors and mitigation techniques
Dataset_or_Testbed: Published amplification attack and defense literature
Measure_Used: Bandwidth amplification factor (BAF) and mitigation deployment feasibility
Main_Finding: Readily available DDoS-for-hire tools and open reflectors enable low-resource attackers to saturate victim links
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Primary mitigations rely on ISP ingress filtering (BCP38) outside website owners' control

Authors: T. V. Phan et al. (Verify exact author list against publisher record)
Title: A survey and meta-analysis of application-layer distributed denial-of-service attack
Problem_Addressed: Stealthy Layer-7 DDoS attacks mimicking legitimate HTTP/HTTPS user behavior
Method: Literature survey and meta-analysis of Layer-7 attack and detection methods
Measure_Used: Detection accuracy, false-positive rate, computational complexity
Main_Finding: Application-layer attacks exhaust server CPU/memory and database resources without triggering volumetric alarms
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Studies prioritize classifier accuracy over operational cost and outage duration on small web stacks

Authors: Author Verification Required (See Wiley/Hindawi DOI 10.1155/2019/1283472)
Title: Review of recent detection methods for HTTP DDoS attack
Problem_Addressed: Difficulty distinguishing HTTP request floods and slow-rate attacks from flash crowds
Method: Comparative survey of statistical, behavioral, and ML-based HTTP detection schemes
Measure_Used: Detection latency, false-positive rate, scalability
Main_Finding: Behavioral and session-based metrics improve HTTP flood separation but increase processing overhead
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Lacks evaluation on low-cost shared hosting or resource-constrained CMS deployments

Authors: A. Bhardwaj, V. Mangat, R. Vig, S. Halder, and M. Conti
Title: Distributed denial of service attacks in cloud: State-of-the-art of scientific and commercial solutions
Problem_Addressed: Gap between academic cloud DDoS defenses and commercial cloud mitigation offerings
Method: Comparative taxonomy of academic prototypes and commercial cloud scrubbing services
Dataset_or_Testbed: Academic literature and commercial platform specifications
Measure_Used: Mitigation layer, deployment model, scalability, operational overhead
Main_Finding: Commercial cloud/CDN providers offer strong volumetric absorption, whereas academic proposals focus on detection algorithms
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Does not quantify total cost of ownership or configuration barriers for small independent operators

Authors: S. Kaur, K. Kumar, N. Aggarwal, and G. Singh
Title: A comprehensive survey of DDoS defense solutions in SDN: Taxonomy, research challenges, and future directions
Problem_Addressed: Controller saturation and flow-table exhaustion in SDN-based DDoS mitigation
Method: Survey of statistical, ML, and entropy-based SDN defense architectures
Measure_Used: Detection accuracy, controller overhead, mitigation response time
Main_Finding: Programmable SDN control planes enable rapid flow-rule mitigation but introduce controller bottlenecks
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Most evaluated solutions assume enterprise SDN infrastructure not available to typical website owners

Authors: A. S. M. Rizvi, L. Bertholdo, J. Ceron, and J. Heidemann
Title: Anycast agility: Network playbooks to fight DDoS
Venue: Proceedings of the 31st USENIX Security Symposium
Problem_Addressed: Localized site overload during large volumetric DDoS attacks on anycast deployments
Method: Active internet measurement and BGP routing playbook evaluation on anycast testbed
Dataset_or_Testbed: PEERING BGP testbed and real-world DDoS stress experiments
Measure_Used: Traffic distribution balance, latency impact, collateral damage
Main_Finding: Dynamic BGP routing playbooks (path prepending, community filtering) redistribute attack traffic across edge sites
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Requires BGP/anycast control possessed by CDNs and large operators rather than single-origin websites

Authors: J. F. Balarezo, S. Wang, K. Gomez Chavez, A. Al-Hourani, and S. Kandeepan
Title: A survey on DoS/DDoS attacks mathematical modelling for traditional, SDN and virtual networks
Venue: Engineering Science and Technology, an International Journal
Problem_Addressed: Need for analytical models to predict resource exhaustion in traditional and virtualized networks
Method: Review of queuing theory, game-theoretic, and epidemic mathematical models
Measure_Used: Queue delay, packet drop probability, system availability
Main_Finding: Mathematical models quantify how finite buffer and CPU capacities degrade rapidly under burst arrivals
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Abstracted analytical models omit real-world operational friction and human response delays

Authors: Q. Li et al.
Title: A comprehensive survey on DDoS defense systems: New trends and challenges
Problem_Addressed: Evolving multi-vector DDoS trends across SDN, NFV, cloud, and AI-assisted defense systems
Method: Literature survey of modern defense architectures and emerging threat trends
Measure_Used: Detection accuracy, architectural adaptability, scalability
Main_Finding: Hybrid cloud-edge and programmable network defenses improve adaptability against multi-vector campaigns
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Limited reporting of end-to-end service downtime and small-organization affordability

Authors: W. Hill et al.
Title: DDoS in SDN: A review of open datasets, attack vectors and mitigation strategies
Problem_Addressed: Reproducibility and dataset limitations in SDN DDoS detection research
Method: Review of open DDoS datasets, attack vectors, and SDN mitigation pipelines
Dataset_or_Testbed: Open benchmark datasets (CICDDoS2019, InSDN, UNSW-NB15, etc.)
Measure_Used: Dataset coverage, feature quality, evaluation metrics
Main_Finding: Heavy reliance on synthetic/simulated SDN testbeds limits generalizability to production networks
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Highlights simulation-to-production gap without empirical SME deployment trials

Authors: M. F. Arroyabe, C. F. A. Arranz, I. F. de Arroyabe, and J. C. F. de Arroyabe
Title: Exploring the economic role of cybersecurity in SMEs: A case study of the UK
Problem_Addressed: Economic and market barriers causing cybersecurity underinvestment in SMEs
Method: Empirical econometric analysis of UK SME survey data
Measure_Used: Cybersecurity investment propensity, risk perception, market failure indicators
Main_Finding: Information asymmetry, low perceived incident probability, and budget constraints drive underinvestment in SMEs
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Examines general SME cybersecurity spending rather than website-specific DDoS outcomes

Authors: R. Wainwright, M. Bagheri, A. Salama, and R. Saatchi
Title: Software-defined networking security detection strategies and their limitations with a focus on distributed denial-of-service for small to medium-sized enterprises
Problem_Addressed: Practical feasibility of SDN-based DDoS detection for resource-constrained SMEs
Method: Targeted literature review of SDN DDoS detection limitations for SMEs
Measure_Used: Deployment complexity, hardware/software cost, SME readiness
Main_Finding: Academic SDN defenses are largely validated in simulations and remain too complex and costly for live SME environments
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Identifies lack of matched empirical comparisons between SME and enterprise networks

Authors: M. Tsiodra, S. Panda, M. Chronopoulos, and E. Panaousis
Title: Cyber risk assessment and optimization: A small business case study
Problem_Addressed: Optimal allocation of strictly limited cybersecurity budgets in small businesses
Method: Quantitative cyber risk assessment and budget optimization case study
Dataset_or_Testbed: Small business operational and threat profile
Measure_Used: Expected loss reduction vs. security control implementation cost
Main_Finding: Small operators face severe trade-offs between core operational expenses and preventive security controls
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Single-organization case study focused on general risk optimization rather than live DDoS stress testing

Authors: C. Rombaldo Junior, I. Becker, and S. D. Johnson
Title: Unaware, unfunded, untrained, and unsupported: A systematic review of cybersecurity in small and medium enterprises
Problem_Addressed: Structural and human factors impeding cybersecurity adoption in SMEs
Method: Systematic literature review
Measure_Used: Frequency and nature of organizational barriers
Main_Finding: Low awareness, insufficient funding, lack of technical training, and weak external support systematically hinder SME resilience
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Broad SME scope without isolated empirical measurements of independent website availability

Authors: Qurium Media Foundation
Title: A 50TB hug to Kloop Media: Forensic analysis of the DDoS attack targeting Kloop.kg
Problem_Addressed: Multi-vector DDoS campaign targeting an independent news organization
Method: Forensic network traffic capture and protocol analysis
Dataset_or_Testbed: 7-hour attack starting Aug 31, 2026 (~50 TB estimated total; ~10 TB analyzed sample)
Measure_Used: Traffic volume, protocol mix (GRE, TCP/HTTPS, TCP ACK, UDP), observed source IPs (~15,000)
Main_Finding: Independent media can face massive multi-vector attacks; specialist upstream support (Qurium) proved critical to resilience
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Single-incident forensic report; observed IPs reflect spoofing/reflection rather than confirmed distinct hosts

Authors: NEMO
Title: How elTOQUE withstood its second DDoS attack in less than a year
Problem_Addressed: Repeated multi-day application-layer DDoS campaign against an independent media outlet
Method: Operational incident post-mortem
Dataset_or_Testbed: Multi-day attack telemetry (hundreds of millions of automated requests)
Measure_Used: Request volume, campaign duration, site availability
Main_Finding: Sustained application-layer floods repeatedly target independent publishers, requiring hardened caching and external support
Stated_or_Observed_Limitation: Operational incident summary rather than peer-reviewed empirical benchmark
